sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Completed conditional review: BQS 5.32, growth-quality GQS 6.05, IAS 4.28. Central return is 10.2%, below the 15% research hurdle. Historical strengths do not remove concentration, capital-allocation, funding or liquidity risks. This is a watchlist assessment, not a buy recommendation. [S1, S2, M1]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026, Axiom Gas Engineering Limited, ISIN INE16J201028, is listed on NSE Emerge from September 25. Admission confirms 35,344,000 shares and a 2,000-share lot. Financial scope is standalone restated FY24–FY26. October 19 close ₹40.90 is dated, not live or guaranteed executable; October 20 was an exchange holiday. All four gates are assessed separately below. Current security eligibility, including additional markets, is considered; price-discovery status is not suspension. [S1, S2, M1, M_SECURITY_SPEC]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 6, DUR 5, CAP 7, CASH 7, BAL 6, EXEC 6 and EARN 6. IAS uses final BQS as Q plus R 3, D 4, P 4 and L 7. Weighted arithmetic, evidence links and contradictory evidence are in the score audit. All scores are Medium confidence; no forecast is portrayed as a measured outcome.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: The company buys LPG for distribution, storage/bottling and auto LPG dispensing stations (ALDS). Economics depend on procurement terms, outlet volumes, logistics, safety compliance and local fuel alternatives. It is not an upstream gas producer. [S1]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Top three suppliers represented 99.75%, 99.42% and 96.87% of purchases in FY26, FY25 and FY24. This may aid purchasing scale but creates dependence on availability and terms. No evidence reviewed establishes durable pricing power against CNG, petrol or electric alternatives. [S1] Prospectus-selected peers are Confidence Petroleum and Aegis Logistics, using July 22 prices and consolidated financials versus standalone Axiom. Larger mixed businesses are imperfect comparators; no peer multiple is imported as fair value. [S1, p 103]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Standalone revenue rose from ₹74.538 crore in FY24 to ₹89.8383 crore and ₹100.7582 crore, a 16.27% two-year CAGR. FY26 goods revenue of ₹100.7582 crore rose 17.23% from ₹85.9473 crore. FY25 also contained ₹1.641 crore outlet-signing fees and ₹2.25 crore consultancy, absent in FY26. Thus total growth understates goods growth, but neither measure isolates volume from LPG prices. The storage-utilization table is not treated as a verified annual dispensing-volume series. PAT was ₹5.7408 crore, ₹7.7494 crore and ₹9.4535 crore. [S1, MD&A and restated statements]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Net IPO proceeds of ₹44.2226 crore allocate ₹27.60 crore to capex, ₹9.1245 crore to debt repayment and ₹7.4981 crore to general purposes. Of ₹18 crore ALDS allocation, ₹4.5213 crore reimburses prior expenditure and ₹13.4787 crore funds remaining cost. Therefore not all IPO capex allocation represents future physical investment. Five of twelve planned stations were already commissioned and another approximately 75% complete at the prospectus date. Estimates were not bank-appraised. [S1, pp 74–76] Capital-return work now includes a transparent endpoint proxy rather than treating unavailable station/cohort returns as an automatic NS. Endpoint ΔNOPAT/ΔIC proxy is 30.8%, or 25.0% after restoring FY24 director remuneration. Both exceed assumed 12–16% capital cost; dealer-deposit inclusion and CWIP tests remain supportive. Contrary evidence: new IPO-funded station cohorts are unseasoned, and endpoint changes are not project IRRs; no 9–10 score. [S1; E_CAP] The September 25 announcement proposes petrol/diesel expansion, terminal projects and an expected import, with unquantified financial impact and required approvals. No incremental profit is credited in the central model; ₹10 crore and ₹25 crore additional capital-allocation stresses are illustrative, not company budgets. [S3]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Related Prime Fuel Logistics supplied transport of ₹3.7957 crore in FY26, versus ₹4.30 crore and ₹3.662 crore previously; the group provides the majority of transport. Review arm’s-length tariffs, alternatives and outstanding advances rather than assuming routine related-party dealings are harmless. Prospectus discloses ROC filing discrepancies requiring item-specific follow-through. [S1] Final-prospectus promoter/group ownership is 72.15% post issue. Director remuneration fell from ₹1.44 crore in FY24 to ₹0.8365 crore in FY25 and ₹0.4838 crore in FY26; normalization should test why, rather than credit the margin gain automatically. Company litigation summary lists five tax and two regulatory matters totaling ₹0.8236 crore, including maximum statutory penalties for compounding applications, not adjudicated liability. Group litigation is separately disclosed and must not be attributed as a company conviction. [S1] FY26 related supplier advances total ₹5.9931 crore, of which Czar Metric System accounts for ₹5.5581 crore, versus ₹5.0207 crore in FY25. The latter equals 16.7% of FY26 equity; the 25% cash-replacement stress is not a reported impairment. Initial September 23 shareholding shows 72.15% promoter ownership, no declared promoter pledge, and 76.44% of all shares locked. These are dated initial disclosures, not October free-float verification. [S1, S2, S4]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY24–FY26 CFO was ₹4.7058 crore, ₹8.1677 crore and ₹10.795 crore. Ratio-of-sums CFO/PAT is 1.032×. The cash-flow presentation includes increases or repayments of long-term liabilities inside operations; their nature should be established before endorsing normalized conversion. FY26 cash capex was about ₹1.996 crore and CWIP cash spend ₹1.7586 crore, compared with ₹3.0037 crore and ₹1.4762 crore in FY25. Separate station reimbursements from new capital needs. [S1] Other long-term liabilities are dealer security deposits, ₹11.803 crore FY26. Thus their operating classification is economically different from bank borrowing; do not mechanically strip them as financing. Deposits can fund operations but carry refund obligations and are not permanent equity. FY26 financial debt was ₹16.0597 crore and cash ₹5.8896 crore before IPO; debt-repayment objects are not proof of subsequent discharge. [S1] Opening operating working capital includes supplier, employee and GST advances and other operating liabilities, totaling ₹19.8816 crore after employee provisions. FY26 cash of ₹5.8896 crore contains ₹4.1733 crore cash in hand; the model separately removes this amount in a funding sensitivity without alleging it is missing. Demand borrowing of ₹2.9521 crore is also tested as an immediate payment reducing cash and debt together. [S1, notes I.20–I.22 and risk factor 8] Opening tax provision ₹2.4994 crore is conservatively settled before the first modeled year. Employee provision ₹0.0078 crore is included in operating liabilities, giving opening operating working capital ₹19.8816 crore. Future modeled taxes are only on future profit, so this opening settlement is not double-counted. [S1] Opening-claim audit: operating statutory, payroll and expense liabilities of ₹1.0595 crore and current employee/expense provisions of ₹0.0078 crore are already included in opening and forecast operating WC. They are not charged again as separate debt. Opening tax/interest settlement remains ₹2.4994 crore. Noncurrent employee liabilities of ₹0.1421 crore are outside operating WC and are now deducted once from terminal equity, held at the opening net obligation with no assumed plan-asset recovery. Future service cost remains within forecast operating expenses. The ₹0.3159 crore opening deferred-tax liability is separately reserved once at terminal. Forecast tax at 25.17% of future positive PBT does not model legacy tax-basis reversals; this reserve is a conservative timing assumption, not a cash tax currently due. Deferred-tax assets receive no cash credit. If legacy reversal is explicitly included in future cash taxes, this reserve must be released to avoid duplication. Existing bank principal remains in the debt schedule and terminal debt; no duplicate current-maturity deduction is made. Dealer security deposits ₹11.8030 crore are already covered by bear refunds and the residual terminal claim, not omitted or charged twice. [S1]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Corrected actual-opening model includes all identified opening tax, interest and operating provision claims. Bear/base/bull conditional IRRs are -12.9%/10.2%/29.1%. Central five-year assumptions and annual cash, debt and dilution schedules are in the valuation model. At central operating performance, a 15% hurdle requires approximately 12.6 times terminal EV/EBIT. The prior optimistic case remains separately labeled. Opening tax provision ₹2.4994 crore is conservatively settled before the first modeled year. Employee provision ₹0.0078 crore is included in operating liabilities, giving opening operating working capital ₹19.8816 crore. Future modeled taxes are only on future profit, so this opening settlement is not double-counted. [S1, S2, M1] The terminal bridge additionally retains the audited legacy employee and deferred-tax claims; the annual operating and financing schedules are unchanged. [S1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Telangana contributed 60.42% of FY26 revenue, Maharashtra 31.39% and Karnataka 8.19%. A local fuel-demand shock, supplier interruption or safety/licence failure could affect a concentrated network. New outlets may dilute returns if fixed costs precede utilization; group logistics dependence creates another operational and governance channel. [S1] Ordinary bear terminal value implies a 49.8% equity loss. Simultaneous margin, working-capital, capex and financing stress is more severe; a modeled equity rescue is conditional and can fail. Advance replacement, cash availability and unbudgeted terminal costs are independently stressed.

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five-year 5× and 10× outcomes require annualized per-share returns of 37.97% and 58.49%. Recent revenue growth of 12.15% alone does not support such outcomes. A defensible case would require higher station productivity and attractive new-station returns without excessive dilution, not merely additional outlets.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track station commissioning, same-station throughput and procurement spread; actual IPO deployment; related supplier advance settlement and replenishment; cash-in-hand reconciliation; dealer refunds; demand-loan calls; and quantified approvals/funding for proposed terminal and petrol/diesel expansion. September 25 expected an import within three weeks, but the reviewed subsequent October 5 filings do not verify completion. REG1 effective October 21 flags SME trading regularity; it does not prove missing sessions or wrongdoing. [S1–S5, M_REG1, M_REG1_FORMAT]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed conditional watchlist review. Better reported cash conversion does not offset all concentration and capital-allocation risks. The central return is below the research hurdle, while ordinary bear valuation impairment is substantial. Re-underwrite after verified outlet economics, advance recovery and investment funding; no trade or position-size recommendation is made.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Financial statements, notes, business history, risk factors, IPO objects, admission/shareholding and available post-listing announcements were reviewed. Estimates use dated actuals and explicit IPO adjustments. Remaining uncertainties are post-IPO deployment, volume versus price, related advance aging/recovery, reported cash availability, contractual debt timing, terminal-project scope and live market depth. These are bounded or stressed rather than silently treated as known. Primary prospectus peer figures are historical and scope-mismatched; no current peer-derived target is asserted. [S1–S5, M1]

GOV.reason: Related supplier advances of ₹5.9931 crore and dependence on related logistics require capital-allocation discipline. The largest advance, ₹5.5581 crore, is 16.7% of FY26 equity. These disclosed balances and historical compliance weaknesses support a below-average stewardship score, not an inference of diversion. Director remuneration declined, providing contrary evidence.

MOAT.reason: Operating outlets and LPG infrastructure provide useful positioning, but near-total supplier concentration and substitutable transport fuel constrain bargaining power. No demonstrated durable excess economics.

REV.reason: Same-scope FY24–FY26 revenue CAGR is 16.27%, mapping to 7 before a one-point adjustment for LPG price/pass-through uncertainty and non-recurring FY25 service revenue. FY26 goods revenue rose 17.23%; total growth of 12.15% was diluted by the absence of prior fees. No unsupported annual dispensing-volume series is inferred.

DUR.reason: Specified outlet pipeline and partial commissioning demonstrate accessible expansion; regional concentration and fuel substitution constrain durability. More stations are not automatically profitable demand.

CAP.reason: Endpoint ΔNOPAT/ΔIC proxy is 30.8%, or 25.0% after restoring FY24 director remuneration. Both exceed assumed 12–16% capital cost; dealer-deposit inclusion and CWIP tests remain supportive. Contrary evidence: new IPO-funded station cohorts are unseasoned, and endpoint changes are not project IRRs; no 9–10 score.

CASH.reason: Three-year reported CFO/PAT is 1.032 times with shrinking receivables. Dealer deposits are operating funding rather than bank debt but refundable; substantial inventory and related advances temper the result. Forecasts assume no additional dealer funding.

BAL.reason: Proforma cash of ₹38.4883 crore after opening tax settlement and bank debt of ₹6.9352 crore support planned capex and ordinary bear debt service. Demand borrowing of ₹2.9521 crore and dealer deposits of ₹11.803 crore remain claims; cash-in-hand availability and terminal expansion are separately stressed. No committed future facility is assumed.

EXEC.reason: Five planned stations commissioned and one substantially advanced provide delivery evidence, but six remain and cost estimates lack independent appraisal; limited post-IPO track record prevents stronger score.

EARN.reason: PAT growth accompanies revenue and other income is negligible; contrary evidence includes substantial remuneration reduction and post-IPO share dilution. Margin persistence not assumed.

R.reason: Central conditional five-year IRR 10.20% after all identified opening claims is -4.80 percentage points below/above the 15% hurdle, mapping to R=3. Forecasts and terminal tax timing remain assumptions.

D.reason: Ordinary bear terminal equity loss is 50.0%. Severe combined operating and financing stress requires conditional rescue and can cause worse loss if financing fails. IPO cash supports ordinary operations, not the quoted equity value.

P.reason: Central operating performance requires approximately 12.6 times terminal EV/EBIT to earn the 15% hurdle, above the central exit assumption. Stronger growth, margin or rerating must bridge the gap; the prior optimistic scenario is not the central case.

L.reason: Sixteen post-listing sessions give conservative median daily turnover of ₹65.2705 lakh and 1.53 illustrative exit days at 5% participation. Starting band 9 is reduced to 7 for short history, ₹81,800 board-lot granularity, substantial initial lock-ins and unobserved live spread/depth. Two and ten percent participation imply 3.83 and 0.77 days.

sensitivities.interpretation: Alternative assumption only. Opening employee claim and all other claims remain deducted.

assumptions: All money is INR crore and share counts are crore shares. FY26 standalone actuals plus net IPO proceeds form a proforma opening, not an observed October balance sheet. Five full modeled years approximate October 2026 to October 2031; no interim dividends.

Opening operating working capital is inventory 16.5583 + receivables 0.7843 + supplier advances 7.3981 + employee advances 0.0193 + GST 0.1598 − payables 3.9709 − other current liabilities 1.0595 − employee provision 0.0078 = 19.8816. Finance/tax receivables and interest receivable are excluded. Opening tax provision is settled separately.

Net IPO funds 44.2226 are credited once; intended debt repayment 9.1245 reduces both cash and debt. Remaining project cash cost 23.8394 excludes reimbursement of historical spend. A separate 4.9318 cash-use stress bounds overlap with March CWIP. GCP 7.4981 is conservatively spent once in year one, not credited again.

Base revenue grows 10%, below FY26 goods growth of 17.23%, allowing for LPG price variability and slower ramp-up while partially commissioned outlets mature. Base EBIT margin 13% is below FY26 14.13%, partially normalizing reduced director and wage costs. No revenue or profit from the unquantified petrol, diesel or terminal proposals is credited.

Growth capex is the greater of the remaining project schedule (70% then 30%) and incremental sales divided by assumed incremental fixed-asset turnover. Maintenance equals modeled depreciation. Depreciation adds growth assets over ten years with a half-year convention; project and marginal capacity costs are not double-counted.

Annual operating cash is PAT + depreciation − change in working capital. Tax is 25.17% on positive PBT. Initial bank debt amortizes evenly over five years as a transparent stress convention, not a contractual schedule. Half-year interest on repayments and new borrowing solves financing circularity.

Cash floor is 5% of sales. Conditional debt capacity is 30% of sales, followed by fallback equity issued at half the observed quote if needed. These are modeled financing mechanisms, not committed facilities. A failure to obtain finance means curtailment or distress, not assured rescue.

Refundable dealer deposits of 11.803 are deducted as debt-like terminal claims; bear refunds 20% in year one. No incremental dealer funding is assumed. Terminal enterprise value is year-five EBIT times an assumed multiple; deduct bank debt and remaining deposits, add cash above the operating floor, divide by diluted shares.

Bear/base/bull exit multiples of 7/10/14 are analyst assumptions, not current peer multiples. Base compares with approximately 8.6 times FY26 EBIT on the IPO-adjusted enterprise-value bridge including deposits. No scenario probabilities are assigned or required for the conditional central-case return score.

FY26 reported cash includes 4.1733 of cash in hand. Its physical availability is not independently verified; an explicit no-credit sensitivity removes it. The related supplier advance replacement stress is a cash-loss sensitivity, not an allegation or reported impairment.

gates.reason: Related supplier balances, transport dependence and historical compliance discrepancies warrant a low governance score and follow-up. Reviewed evidence does not substantiate severe diversion or minority abuse. Disclosure is not a guarantee of recovery.

Restated standalone statements, related-party detail and cash bridge support a usable baseline. Advance recoverability and reported cash in hand are stressed; no unsupported dispensing-volume series or prospective terminal revenue is treated as actual.

IPO-adjusted funding supports the existing project in ordinary bear and central cases. Demand repayment, advance replacement, cash availability and additional terminal investment are tested. Severe stress may require uncommitted finance, so shareholder recovery is not assured.

Official trades and additional-market eligibility corroborate trading. A ₹5 lakh reference is 6.11 lots; six lots cost ₹490,800. Sixteen sessions cannot establish 60-session liquidity or live depth; initial lock-ins and REG1 caution remain relevant.
